messages.subject: Recoding the values in dataset
parts:
Hi, I have a query... I need to recode the levels in data set with "A"
as 10, "B" as 11 and so on...
The variable is a factor variable , so tried using the "levels ". but
then i want to run the same for whole data set irrespective of the
value is being there in that column or not....
I need a substitute of "find and replace" function as in Excel as in
R.

Thanks & Regards,

Subha.R

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Recoding the values in dataset
parts:
This works for your example, with "A"->10, "B"->11, etc. - is that
what you meant?

# your factor
set.seed(1)
the.factor<-factor(sample(LETTERS[1:4], 20, replace=T))
the.factor

# recode
recoded<-as.numeric(the.factor)+9
recoded

# check
table(recoded, the.factor)

Cheers,
STG

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: Recoding the values in dataset
parts:
Well, either you read in the files as character vectors with scan and
use gsub on them (e.g., with a loop), or, if they all look like this,
...

# create factors
set.seed(1)

lev<-c(1:9, LETTERS[1:13])
f1<-factor(sample(lev, 30, replace=T))
f2<-factor(sample(lev, 30, replace=T))
f3<-factor(sample(lev, 30, replace=T))

# create two identical data frames with these factors
df<-df2<-data.frame(f1,f2,f3)

# look at the data frame df
lapply(df, table)
df

... then you can use the same logic as in my last response:

# recode the factors in df2
for (i in seq(df)) {
levels(df2[,i])[levels(df2[,i]) %in%
LETTERS]<-match(levels(df2[,i])[which(levels(df2[,i]) %in% LETTERS)],
LETTERS)+9
}

# look at the result
lapply(df2, table) # done
df2 # done
table(df[,1], df2[,1]) # done


Without a concrete example of what the data look like, it's hard to
write something that will cover all possibilities, though.

STG
